key_facts: 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on the face
History of left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier
Treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy
Left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision seven years after initial diagnosis
Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek
Predominantly involving the left side of the face
Histopathological examination showed hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis
Immunohistochemical examination showed epithelial cells in dilated vessels positive for CD31 and atypical cells positive for GATA3

raw.rationale: The patient's history of breast carcinoma, the presence of violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the face, and the immunohistochemical examination showing atypical cells positive for GATA3 (a marker for breast cancer) support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous metastatic breast carcinoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of breast carcinoma, the specific presentation of telangiectasia and the immunohistochemical findings better support TMBC.

rejected.label: Carcinoma en cuirasse
rejected.why: This condition typically presents as a diffuse, infiltrative, and indurated lesion, which does not match the patient's presentation of violaceous swelling with telangiectasia.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: Although the histopathological examination showed dilated vessels with atypical cells, the presence of GATA3 positivity suggests a breast cancer origin rather than a primary angiosarcoma.

rejected.label: Postradiation angiosarcoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of radiotherapy, the clinical and immunohistochemical findings are more consistent with metastatic breast carcinoma than a radiation-induced angiosarcoma.
